display.title: The Silver Mirror
display.summary_short: A generous man asks a Rebbe for wealth so he can give more tzedakah, but riches make him a miser, until the Rebbe shows him the difference between a window and a mirror.
display.summary_long: Reb Avraham is a kind, hard-working man who always welcomes guests and gives tzedakah with an open hand. When a great Rebbe stays at his home, Reb Avraham asks for a blessing of wealth so he can give even more. The Rebbe warns him that riches can change a person's nature, but blesses him. As his business grows, Reb Avraham stops davening in shul, drops his evening learning, and sends his maid to turn the poor away with a few coins. Within a year he is known as a selfish miser. The Rebbe returns and stands him before a window, where he sees the poor water carrier, woodchopper and cobbler, and then before a mirror, where he sees only himself. Both are glass, the Rebbe explains, but the mirror is coated with silver. Reb Avraham weeps, does teshuvah, returns to his good ways, and gives more tzedakah than ever.
display.lesson: Do not let wealth, the 'silver', blind you to others; riches are a blessing only when they are shared.
